//: TYPE-CHECK FOR THE COPILOT UAT SCORING DECISION (#4432 follow-up, review F5).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `tsconfig.build.json` excludes `e2e/**`,
`**/__tests__/**` and `*.test.ts`, and vitest transpiles with esbuild and
type-checks nothing. So the headline 'tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.build.json'
receipt covers the routes and the client and reads NONE of the files that
hold the scoring decision this change is about: `e2e/_lib/copilot-verdict.ts`,
the two UAT specs, and the three suites that pin them. That is the same gap
#3963 found for the brain specs, and the same answer: a narrow generated
tsconfig that a compiler actually reads.
THREE CONTROLS, because a type-check over an empty glob is green and blind.
They live in scripts/ci/check-copilot-decision-types.mjs:
1. POPULATION — `--listFilesOnly` first, REFUSING below 7 matched
decision files (measured at 7 on the branch that added this).
2. KNOWN-RED BY FILE, NEVER BY DIRECTORY — exactly two files are
allowed to fail, both for the SAME pre-existing cause the brain-spec
step already records: `lib/azure/azure-sql-client.ts` and
`lib/azure/synapse-sql-client.ts` import `mssql`, which ships no
types (TS7016). They arrive transitively, not from anything here.
An earlier draft of this comment claimed NO known-red list; that was
false the moment it was written, and saying so is cheaper than
letting a comment assert a property the code does not have.
3. THE LIST MUST SHRINK — if a known-red file starts compiling clean the
check FAILS telling you to delete its entry.
`e2e/**` is normally excluded because the Playwright specs are not part of
the Next build; including them HERE is the point — `copilot.uat.ts` is where
the scoring decision is applied, and a rename there silently removing a
persona from the must-answer rule is precisely the defect class this PR is
fixing one layer down.
